nodes.label: Response Envelope Interceptor Ordering
nodes.rationale: AuditLogInterceptor is registered after ResponseFormatInterceptor precisely so audit snapshots the plain DTO and the formatter wraps afterwards; Nest unwinds interceptors in reverse registration order, so swapping them would have audit recording envelopes.

nodes.label: ScopeGuard / assertFactoryScope Dual Implementation
nodes.rationale: ScopeGuard covers routes that name their factory in the request; services use assertFactoryScope() because most routes identify the factory only after loading the entity. Both refuse with 403; no service re-derives the check.

nodes.label: Stock Ledger Invariants (Three Layers)
nodes.rationale: Conditional compare-and-set decrement prevents concurrent over-issue; database CHECK constraints (quantity>=0, reserved<=quantity, movement quantity>0) enforce non-negativity since Prisma cannot express them; every balance change writes a stock_movements row in the same transaction so a retry cannot inflate stock.

nodes.label: Audit Logging Mechanism
nodes.rationale: AuditLogInterceptor writes an audit_logs row for LOGIN, CREATE_EXCHANGE, APPROVE_CONFIRMATION, REJECT_CONFIRMATION, ISSUE_NEEDLE, TRANSFER_STOCK, ADJUST_STOCK, CHANGE_MASTER, CHANGE_CONFIGURATION, DEVICE_BIND, DEVICE_REVOKE. Only successful actions are recorded; row written before response release but as a separate write from the handler transaction.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key / client_transaction_id Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Critical commands (create exchange, issue, complete, approval, receiving, transfer, return, adjustment, sync) accept Idempotency-Key/client_transaction_id and return the same result on retry, single implementation in IdempotencyKeyMiddleware. Reusing a key with a different body returns 422; a concurrent retry returns 409.

nodes.label: Five-Dimension Authorization Model
nodes.rationale: User, Role+Permission, Factory scope, Location scope, Action. Permission codes match as exact strings and imply nothing else.

nodes.label: ADR-003 Trolley Is an Inventory Location
nodes.norm_label: adr-003 trolley is an inventory location
nodes.rationale: Every trolley is a stock location in its own right, not merely a device; supports 3 trolleys per factory, configurable trolley counts, transfer, per-trolley monitoring, and reconciliation. A trolley owns a TROLLEY-typed location rather than holding stock directly.

nodes.label: ADR-005 Offline-First Android
nodes.rationale: Commands arrive out of order and repeat because production-floor network availability cannot be assumed; every critical command is idempotent (Idempotency-Key / client_transaction_id).

nodes.label: ADR-006 WhatsApp Is the Only Notification Channel
nodes.norm_label: adr-006 whatsapp is the only notification channel
nodes.rationale: Outbound only; it notifies but never triggers a mutation, which is why WhatsAppPort has no receive method. Approval must occur through an authenticated secure system page, preventing transaction mutation via messaging channel.

nodes.label: AADR-001 Two Client Applications
nodes.rationale: Android optimized for production-floor transaction speed; WebApp optimized for administration, inventory, monitoring, and analytics.

nodes.label: AADR-002 Shared Backend
nodes.rationale: Both clients use one Central Backend to avoid different business rules and different transaction authorities.

nodes.label: AADR-003 Mobile Offline-First
nodes.rationale: Mobile supports local transaction and synchronization because production-floor network availability cannot be assumed.

nodes.label: AADR-004 Hardware Adapter
nodes.rationale: RFID and Camera use adapter boundaries so hardware can change without modifying domain logic.

nodes.label: AADR-005 No Direct Database Access
nodes.rationale: Mobile and WebApp never access PostgreSQL directly, for security, authorization, consistency, audit, and centralized business rules.

nodes.label: Exchange State Machine (Pure Function)
nodes.rationale: exchange-state-machine.ts imports neither Prisma nor Nest; takes a context and action and returns the states-path to write or throws, so all 41 tests run without a database. Returns a path, not a single state, and owns requiresStockReversal()/NON_TERMINAL_STATES so adding a state cannot silently miss them. 'Blocked' is not a persisted state, only a description of a stuck condition.

nodes.label: Side Effects Happen After Commit
nodes.rationale: BullMQ jobs are not rolled back with the database transaction, so enqueuing notifications/audit inside a transaction that later fails would announce an event that never happened; writing after commit means the worst case is a missing notification, not a false one. The stock-blocked notice is queued from the catch block after rollback.

nodes.label: ADR-001 Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: One REST service, one database, modules separated logically by folder (package-by-feature); modules ship together, never their own service/deployment. Chosen because inventory consistency is easier inside a single transaction; module boundaries drawn so a module could be extracted later if scale demands it.

nodes.label: ADR-002 PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL chosen as the DBMS for ACID guarantees, relational inventory model, constraints, reporting fit, and mature ecosystem.

nodes.label: ADR-004 Backend Is the Stock Authority
nodes.norm_label: adr-004 backend is the stock authority
nodes.rationale: Server validates and executes every business rule and stock mutation; data from mobile/web is a claim to re-validate, never truth. Access tokens carry only sub/username/type; roles, permissions and scopes are reloaded per request so a deactivated user or revoked grant takes effect immediately.

nodes.label: Flag Gaps and Conflicts Principle
nodes.rationale: Missing/contradictory endpoint against Docs/12 gets fixed there first, with the user's knowledge, not patched around in the frontend; an ADR contradiction is surfaced explicitly, never silently overridden.

nodes.label: Reuse Before You Build Principle
nodes.rationale: A second StatusBadge implementation is a bug, not a feature; one implementation reused everywhere for components, API client setup, auth handling, and permission-gating logic.
